claims.text: Thermal spraying FeCoNiCrAl feedstock in the 15–45 µm size range produces a bond coat with sub-target thickness.
The 15–45 µm-feedstock baseline maintains acceptable coating integrity.
The 15–45 µm-feedstock baseline has minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention is to replace the 15–45 µm feedstock with approximately 45–75 µm feedstock without changing other spray parameters.
Using approximately 45–75 µm FeCoNiCrAl powder will improve deposition efficiency relative to 15–45 µm powder.
Larger powder particles have greater thermal mass.
Larger powder particles have greater momentum under the proposed unchanged spray conditions.
Larger particles form thicker splats on impact.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger particles minimizes in-flight oxidation.
The coarser particles have enhanced kinetic energy and thermal buffering.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy and thermal buffering improve deposition efficiency and coating buildup.
The coarser feedstock will attain or exceed the required coating thickness relative to the 15–45 µm baseline.
The coarser feedstock will preserve a dense, well-adhered microstructure.
The coarser feedstock will keep as-sprayed oxidation similar to the baseline.
The intervention should remain effective under typical bond-coat thermal-spray conditions and a standard processing atmosphere if the parameters and atmosphere are optimized.
Increasing particle size beyond an optimal window may cause incomplete melting or reduced bonding quality.
A side-by-side comparison on identical substrates, with feedstock size as the only intentionally changed factor, is the proposed controlled experiment.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thickness increase meeting the target, or observation of increased oxidation or degraded integrity, falsifies the hypothesis.
